label: sec:molecular-hecke-algebra-intro
html: This section extends the atomic constructor to multi-atom systems. The molecular braid joins pre-computed atomic braids inside a single Hecke algebra. Inter-atomic crossing coefficients record how strands from different nuclei interact. Two atoms share a single electron trefoil to form a covalent bond. The ILP characterisation of the covalent bond identifies that shared trefoil as the inverse trefoil T_{2,3}^{-1}, the minimum-crossing knot operator with positive binding energy. With these four objects in hand, molecules are computed by Hopf-linking atoms. Unlike synthetic topological stereochemistry — where macroscopic molecular backbones are themselves tied into trefoil knots and catenanes in three-dimensional space, beginning with the synthetic molecular trefoil knot of Christiane O. Dietrich-Buchecker and Jean-Pierre Sauvage [dietrich-buchecker-sauvage1989] and classified via spatial graph chirality by Erica Flapan [flapan2000] — the braids here live in the internal Iwahori--Hecke algebra H_n(q) of the constituent nucleons and shared electrons, modelling ordinary covalent bonds rather than mechanically interlocked macrocycles.
